{{short description|Hungarian mathematician}}
{{western name order|Pintz János}}

'''János Pintz''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈjaːnoʃ ˈpints}}; born 20 December 1950 in [[Budapest]])<ref>Peter Hermann, Antal Pasztor: ''Magyar és nemzetközi ki kicsoda'', 1994</ref> is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] working in [[analytic number theory]]. He is a fellow of the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|Rényi Mathematical Institute]] and is also a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. In 2014, he received the [[Cole Prize]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]].

==Mathematical results==
Pintz is best known for proving in 2005 (with [[Daniel Goldston]] and [[Cem Yıldırım]])<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Goldston | first1=Daniel | last2=Pintz | first2=János | last3=Yıldırım | first3=Cem | title=Primes in tuples I | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=170 | issue=2 | date=1 September 2009 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2009.170.819 | pages=819–862| s2cid=1994756 | doi-access=free }}</ref> that
:: <math>\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{\log p_n}=0</math>
where <math>p_n</math> denotes the ''n''<sup>th</sup> [[prime number]]. In other words, for every ε&nbsp;>&nbsp;0, there exist infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes ''p''<sub>''n''</sub> and ''p''<sub>''n''+1</sub> that are closer to each other than the average distance  between consecutive primes by a factor of ε, i.e., ''p''<sub>''n''+1</sub>&nbsp;−&nbsp;''p''<sub>''n''</sub>&nbsp;<&nbsp;ε&nbsp;log&nbsp;''p''<sub>''n''</sub>. This result was originally reported in 2003 by [[Daniel Goldston]] and [[Cem Yıldırım]] but was later retracted.<ref name="Zhang 2014 pp. 1121–1174">{{cite journal | last=Zhang | first=Yitang | title=Bounded gaps between primes | journal=Annals of Mathematics | volume=179 | issue=3 | date=1 May 2014 | issn=0003-486X | doi=10.4007/annals.2014.179.3.7 | pages=1121–1174| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aimath.org/primegaps/residueerror/ |title=Residueerror |access-date=2009-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090220194401/http://aimath.org/primegaps/residueerror/ |archive-date=2009-02-20 }}</ref> Pintz joined the team and completed the proof in 2005 and developed the so-called [[GPY sieve]]. Later, they improved this to showing that ''p''<sub>''n''+1</sub>&nbsp;−&nbsp;''p''<sub>''n''</sub>&nbsp;<&nbsp;ε{{radic|log&nbsp;''n''}}(log&nbsp;log&nbsp;''n'')<sup>2</sup> occurs infinitely often. Further, if one assumes the [[Elliott–Halberstam conjecture]], then one can also show that primes within 16 of each other occur infinitely often, which is nearly the [[Twin prime|twin prime conjecture]].

Additionally,
* With [[János Komlós (mathematician)|János Komlós]] and [[Endre Szemerédi]], he disproved the [[Heilbronn triangle problem|Heilbronn conjecture]].<ref>{{citation|last1=Komlós|first1=J.|last2=Pintz|first2=J.|last3=Szemerédi|first3=E.|title=A lower bound for Heilbronn's problem|journal=[[Journal of the London Mathematical Society]]|volume=25|issue=1|pages=13–24|year=1982|doi=10.1112/jlms/s2-25.1.13}}.</ref>
* With [[Henryk Iwaniec|Iwaniec]], he proved that for sufficiently large ''n''  there is a prime between ''n'' and ''n''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''n''<sup>23/42</sup>.<ref name="Iwaniec Pintz 1984 pp. 115–143">{{cite journal | last1=Iwaniec | first1=Henryk | last2=Pintz | first2=János | title=Primes in short intervals | journal=Monatshefte für Mathematik | volume=98 | issue=2 | date=1984 | issn=0026-9255 | doi=10.1007/BF01637280 | pages=115–143}}</ref>
* Pintz gave an effective upper bound for the first number for which the [[Mertens conjecture]] fails.<ref name="Pintz 1987 Astérisque">{{cite journal | last=Pintz | first=János | title=An effective disproof of the Mertens conjecture | journal=Astérisque | volume=147-148 | date=1987 | pages=325–333}}</ref>
* He gave an O(''x''<sup>2/3</sup>) upper bound for the number of those numbers that are less than ''x'' and not the sum of two primes.
* With [[Imre Z. Ruzsa]], he improved a result of [[Yuri Linnik|Linnik]] by showing that every sufficiently large even number is the sum of two primes and at most 8 powers of 2.
* Goldston, S. W. Graham, Pintz, and Yıldırım proved that the difference between numbers which are products of exactly 2 primes is infinitely often at most 6.<ref>D. Goldston, S. W. Graham, J. Pintz, C. Yıldırım: Small gaps between products of two primes, [[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society|Proc. Lond. Math. Soc.]], '''98'''(2007) 741–774.</ref>
